Select Columns of a Data Frame Corresponding to a Seasonal Period

Source: R/select_by_season.R
select_by_season.Rd

Keeps the observations that fall within a seasonal range of months: the date columns of a wide table, or the layers of a raster. Identifier columns are kept.

Usage

select_by_season(x, start_month, end_month, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
select_by_season(x, start_month, end_month, ...)

# S3 method for class 'SpatRaster'
select_by_season(x, start_month, end_month, ...)

Arguments

x

A data.frame or tibble with identifier columns and date-labeled columns (e.g. "2021-04-01", "X2022.07.15"), or a SpatRaster with dates.

start_month

The starting month of the seasonal window. Can be provided as an integer (1 to 12), a month abbreviation (e.g., "Apr"), or a full month name (e.g., "April").

end_month

The ending month of the seasonal window. Same format as start_month.

...

Unused.

Value

x restricted to the months of the season. A raster keeps its context.

Details

If start_month <= end_month, the function returns all observations between those two months (inclusive). If start_month > end_month, the season crosses the year boundary (e.g., November to February).

Date columns are those whose name starts with a year, optionally after an X.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  ID = 1,
  "2021-01-01" = 10,
  "2021-04-01" = 15,
  "2021-07-01" = 20,
  "2021-11-01" = 25,
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Select April to July
select_by_season(df, "Apr", "Jul")
#>   ID 2021-04-01 2021-07-01
#> 1  1         15         20

# Select November to February (crosses year boundary)
select_by_season(df, 11, 2)
#>   ID 2021-01-01 2021-11-01
#> 1  1         10         25
